sectors.theme: Haus on 15 launch: Block B sold out as Gamuda Land-Taylor's Assets open Block A of their RM540m GDV SS15 redevelopment

items.headline: Gamuda Land and Taylor's Assets launch Haus on 15 on the former Taylor's College SS15 site - Block B fully sold, Block A opens from RM736,800
items.detail: Gamuda Land and Taylor's Assets officially launched Haus on 15, a 2.88-acre freehold mixed-use development with a gross development value of RM540 million on the former Taylor's College campus in SS15, Subang Jaya. Block B, soft-launched in early October, is fully sold; Block A opened for sale at the launch. The project comprises two 31-storey serviced apartment towers (614 units, 690-980 sq ft, priced from RM736,800), a 253-unit purpose-built student accommodation block (401 beds, retained by Taylor's Assets and managed by Taylor's Hostel Management, serving institutions across Subang Jaya-Sunway) and 18 retail units (1,399-2,829 sq ft, from RM1.52 million). Groundbreaking was in July; completion is slated for 2029.
items.soWhat: A full Block B sell-out within weeks of soft launch signals deep demand for well-located Subang Jaya product; the retained PBSA block gives Taylor's a recurring-income asset anchored to the area's student population.

sectors.theme: Noraini's MEOA speech pushes replanting, mechanisation and MSPO upgrades - no new funding announced

items.headline: Noraini tells planters to replant ageing estates and mechanise; frames MSPO sustainability as competitiveness, not cost
items.detail: Plantations and Commodities Minister Datuk Seri Dr Noraini Ahmad told the Malaysian Estate Owners Association's 95th anniversary celebration that the industry must accelerate productivity and technology adoption to counter rising operating costs, labour shortages and intensifying global competition. She said replanting of ageing estates is necessary to maintain yields but requires substantial financing, time and careful planning, and urged government-industry cooperation on the structural challenge. She positioned Malaysian Sustainable Palm Oil (MSPO) certification as the foundation for meeting international buyers' transparency demands, arguing sustainability should be managed as a competitiveness lever rather than a cost.
items.soWhat: Speech-level direction with no new funding or mandate attached; the signal is continued policy pressure on estates to fund replanting capex and mechanisation - relevant to listed planters' cost curves and to lenders assessing plantation credits.
